title: Cross-SDK transport tuning: request timeouts, connection pooling, and keep-alive ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood SDKs currently expose per-request timeouts and retry helpers, but defaults and transport-level tuning are inconsistent across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Customers running high-throughput streaming and batch workloads report occasional tail-latency spikes and connection churn under heavy load. We need a coordinated cross-SDK initiative to standardize sensible defaults, make connection pooling and keep-alive configuration accessible, document recommended values, and provide ergonomic examples for streaming and long-running requests.

Goals:
- Define a consistent configuration surface across SDKs for request timeouts, dial/connect timeouts, per-request deadlines, connection pooling (max idle/conns), keep-alive/idle timeout, and TLS handshake timeouts.
- Provide safe, well-documented defaults for interactive and high-throughput workloads.
- Add examples for streaming clients (long-lived responses, chunked streaming) that demonstrate timeout management, ping/keep-alive and retry semantics.
- Expose transport-level knobs without breaking backward compatibility.
- Ship tests and perf benchmarks demonstrating improved tail latency and reduced connection churn.

Acceptance criteria:
- Public SDK API surfaces documented in SDK reference for Python/TS/Go with matching names where possible (e.g., TransportConfig / ClientOptions).
- Default values: 60s request deadline for interactive non-stream calls, 0 (disabled) or large for streaming; connect timeout 5s; keep-alive 30s; max idle connections 100 (SDK-level override). Document rationale.
- Retry behavior documented and plumbed to respect per-request deadlines. Retries must not extend beyond the deadline.
- Integration tests that simulate connection drops and verify backoff, keep-alive reuse, and streaming re-connect guidance.
- Benchmarks showing 20% reduction in connection creation rate under a synthetic 10k RPS scenario on dev infra.

Proposed approach by SDK:
- Python (httpx + custom transport):
  - Add ClientConfig.transport_options with keys: connect_timeout, read_timeout, keepalive (seconds), max_keepalive_connections, pool_limits.
  - Default to httpx.Limits with keepalive_expiry=30, max_connections=100.
  - Stream mode: provide StreamContext that disables read_timeout by default and requires an explicit stream_deadline parameter.
  - Ensure retries use deadline-aware wrapper that cancels further attempts when remaining_time <= 0.

- TypeScript (fetch/node http.Agent/browser fetch):
  - Expose fetchTransportOptions on RedwoodClient with agent options for Node (keepAlive, maxSockets, timeout) and clear browser fallback docs.
  - Default node agent: keepAlive=true, keepAliveMsecs=30000, maxSockets=200.
  - Streaming ergonomics: provide readable stream helpers that accept signal and explicit streamingDeadline.

- Go (net/http client):
  - Provide TransportConfig struct with DialContext timeouts, TLSHandshakeTimeout, IdleConnTimeout, MaxIdleConns, MaxIdleConnsPerHost.
  - Default: Dial timeout 5s, TLSHandshake 5s, IdleConnTimeout 30s, MaxIdleConns 100, MaxIdleConnsPerHost 100.
  - Ensure per-request context deadline is respected; retries use context-aware backoff.

Compatibility and configuration precedence:
- Order of precedence: per-call options > client/instance-level config > environment variables > SDK default constants.
- New env var names: REDWOOD_SDK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, REDWOOD_SDK_IDLE_CONN_TIMEOUT, REDWOOD_SDK_MAX_IDLE_CONNS.

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Unit tests for config parsing and precedence.
- Integration test harness that simulates transient TCP resets and long-lived streams.
- Benchmark harness (k6/golang client) to measure connection creation rate, CPU and latency at 1k/5k/10k RPS.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge cross-SDK design doc and API proposals.
2) Implement feature flags behind opt-in config in all three SDKs.
3) Run integration/benchmarks in staging with Dedicated test cluster.
4) Flip opt-in for new defaults after 2-week canary.

Documentation:
- Confluence design doc and example snippets for each SDK.
- Changelog entries and migration guidance for customers with custom transport code.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Changing defaults could affect existing customers with aggressive timeouts; mitigation: feature flag + clear migration doc.
- Exposing low-level transport options may encourage copying platform-level tuning; provide recommended presets (interactive, batch, streaming).
comments: 2026-02-19 - Liam O'Connor: Kicked off initial scoping session with Python/TS/Go leads. Asked to prioritize clear examples for streaming—seems to be the main pain point from support tickets.

2026-02-25 - Priya Singh (SDK PM): Added customer snippets from enterprise customers missing keep-alive settings in node agents (link in attachments). Request to add CI tests for streaming re-connections.

2026-03-02 - Diego Morales (Python lead): Prototype implemented using httpx custom Transport. Observed ~30% fewer TCP connects in local benchmark with keepalive_expiry=30. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/512

2026-03-07 - Code review (TS): Reviewer recommends splitting agent options into AgentPreset enum (interactive|batch|streaming) to avoid combinatorial explosion of knobs. Good UX suggestion—will add presets while keeping advanced transport_options available.

2026-03-10 - Security review (Rina Chen): Transport knobs acceptable. Flagged requirement to ensure TLS handshake timeouts are configurable for slow TLS providers. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-12 - QA (Marco Ng): Integration harness added to staging. Repro script for connection churn attached. Ran 5k RPS test - initial results show 18% reduction in connection churn for Python and 22% for Go when presets enabled.
2026-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Merging cross-SDK design doc to tracking board. Action items: finalize presets, add environment var parsing, land Python PR and start TS/Go implementations next sprint.
